80910.subject: Starknet Puts Its Ethereum Exit to a Vote
80910.body:
**gm, Defiers!**

These are the biggest stories in DeFi and crypto:

* **[Tether](https://thedefiant.io/converge/regulation/tether-routed-payments-to-hines-s-firm-during-white-house-tenure-wsj-reports)**[ paid Bo Hines's firm, WSJ reports](https://thedefiant.io/converge/regulation/tether-routed-payments-to-hines-s-firm-during-white-house-tenure-wsj-reports)

* **[Ledger](https://thedefiant.io/news/security/ledger-blames-organized-group-for-months-long-wallet-tampering-campaign)**[ blamed an organized group for implants](https://thedefiant.io/news/security/ledger-blames-organized-group-for-months-long-wallet-tampering-campaign)

* [**Bitcoin slips **](https://thedefiant.io/news/markets/us-wholesale-inflation-accelerates-to-6-3-as-bitcoin-slips)[as U .S. producer prices rose ](https://thedefiant.io/news/markets/us-wholesale-inflation-accelerates-to-6-3-as-bitcoin-slips)

* **[Starknet](https://thedefiant.io/news/blockchains/starknet-puts-independent-l1-research-to-a-community-vote)**[ opened a vote on L1 research](https://thedefiant.io/news/blockchains/starknet-puts-independent-l1-research-to-a-community-vote)

* **[Russia](https://thedefiant.io/news/regulation/russia-bars-self-custody-withdrawals-from-regulated-crypto-accounts)**[ barred withdrawals to self-custody](https://thedefiant.io/news/regulation/russia-bars-self-custody-withdrawals-from-regulated-crypto-accounts)

Starknet is a Layer 2 network on Ethereum. It runs its own transactions and posts proofs and data to Ethereum, so in principle its users get Ethereum's security. On Oct. 8, StarkWare said it is [weighing a move to become an independent Layer 1](https://thedefiant.io/news/blockchains/starknet-weighs-layer-1-shift-to-pursue-quantum-security-by-2027) that resists quantum computers, with 2027 as the target. On Oct. 10, it called that shift its ["clearest path forward."](https://thedefiant.io/news/blockchains/starkware-calls-starknet-l1-shift-its-clearest-path-forward) Today Starknet opened a poll on whether to research that move. **StarkWare CEO Eli Ben-Sasson explained his reasons **[**on our livestream**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q49tpDpJ7O0)**.** His case rests on one idea: an L2 is only as safe as the chain under it. How much security do Ethereum's L2s take from Ethereum today?

Ben-Sasson's argument starts with quantum risk. A large quantum computer could break the signatures and data commitments that Ethereum uses. "If Ethereum as a layer one is not post-quantum secure, then there's no L2 on Ethereum that is quantum secure," he said. Starknet's own proofs are hash-based, which he says already resists quantum attacks. He doubts Ethereum will upgrade in time, and he said no blockchain is fully post-quantum secure today.

[L2BEAT](https://l2beat.com/scaling/summary) data shows a second dependency. L2BEAT rates rollups in stages, and only at Stage 2 do proofs govern the chain and users get time to exit before an upgrade. Of $41.3 billion on Ethereum L2s today, Stage 2 chains
